status_effects.explanation: The narrator's ironic comic portrait (mouse-and-sugar simile, 'sourire aimanté') lowers her in the reader's estimation, casting her as comically vain and superficially fixated on Swann rather than genuinely engaged.

appraisal_events.evidence: la princesse ne fit plus ... que tourner sa figure ... comme une souris blanche apprivoisée à qui on tend puis on retire un morceau de sucre ... elle déplaçait parallèlement son sourire aimanté
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator mocks the princesse des Laumes (later duchesse de Guermantes) with a comic simile comparing her to a tame mouse chasing sugar, portraying her as trivially absorbed in tracking Swann's presence rather than attending to the music.
